exercises.instruction: Lie on back, arms extended to ceiling, knees at 90°. Lower opposite arm and leg simultaneously, return to start. Alternate sides

exercises.instruction: Start in plank position. Without bending elbows, retract shoulder blades (push body away from floor), then protract (pull body toward floor)

exercises.name: Light Ladder Patterns
exercises.instruction:
Choose 1-2 patterns from the following options. Perform light, controlled movements focusing on rhythm and coordination:

1. SINGLE-IN RHYTHM RUN: Step one foot per square, alternating L-R-L-R. Feet land in center of each square. Keep steps short and quick, not bounding. Exit with smooth 5m acceleration. Cues: "Tap-tap-tap-tap", "Quiet feet, tall posture".

2. DOUBLE-IN QUICK STEPS: Step two feet in each square: L-R → L-R → L-R. Feet land under hips, not wide. Keep cadence fast but controlled. Avoid heel striking - stay on balls of feet. Cues: "Left-right, left-right", "Fast feet, slow body".

3. LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (WARM VERSION): Face sideways. Step in-in (lead foot first), then out-out. Example facing right: R-L in → R-L out. Feet stay parallel, hips square. Move down ladder without crossing legs. Cues: "Push the ground away", "Stay level - no bouncing".

4. ICKY SHUFFLE (LIGHT TEMPO): Step right foot in, left foot in, right foot out. Then left foot in, right foot in, left foot out. Pattern repeats diagonally through ladder. Keep steps small and rhythmic. Cues: "In-in-out, in-in-out", "Eyes up - see the field".

5. HOPSCOTCH (PREP VERSION): Two feet in → one foot out. Alternate landing foot each square. Example: both feet in → right foot out → both feet in → left foot out. Land softly on single leg. Cues: "Land under hips", "Don't let knee cave in".
exercises.definition: Prepares feet and nervous system for agility work. Focus on rhythm, coordination, and CNS wake-up. Intensity: smooth, not fast.
exercises.notes: Choose 1-2 patterns per session, rotating through all 5 over time. Keep it light and controlled. Focus on rhythm, not speed.

exercises.name: Agility Ladder
exercises.instruction:
Continuous agility flow - perform each segment for 30 seconds. Self-time each transition:

0:00-0:30 - FAST DOUBLE-IN: L-R in each square. Feet move like "machine gun taps". Stay tall, minimal vertical bounce. Exit with 3m burst. Rugby transfer: acceleration after footwork.

0:30-1:00 - LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (DEFENSIVE DRIFT): Face sideways. Lead foot steps in first: R-L in → R-L out. Keep shoulders square. Add 2m "tackle finish" at end. Rugby transfer: drift defense, tracking attackers.

1:00-1:30 - ICKY SHUFFLE + SIDESTEP EXIT: In-in-out pattern through ladder. At end, plant outside foot (right or left). Explode into sidestep opposite direction. Rugby transfer: evasive footwork, fend setup.

1:30-2:00 - REACTIVE CALL PATTERN: Self-call pattern - call out to yourself: "IN" → single-in (L-R-L-R), "OUT" → double-out (feet outside ladder each square), "LEFT" or "RIGHT" → lateral shuffle (no crossing feet). Rugby transfer: decision-making under movement.

2:00-2:30 - CROSSOVER STEP (CUTTING PREP): Step across body into each square. Example: right foot crosses over left into square. Keep hips facing forward. Add 3m acceleration at exit. Rugby transfer: sharp angle changes, line breaks.
exercises.definition: Foot-speed, reactive agility, rugby transfer. Intensity: 70-90%
exercises.notes: Self-time each 30-second segment. Focus on foot-speed and rugby-specific movement patterns. Smooth transitions between patterns.

exercises.name: Sun Salutations
exercises.notes: Match breath to movement throughout
exercises.instruction:
Begin in Mountain Pose (Tadasana): Stand tall, feet together, arms at sides, weight evenly distributed
INHALE: Sweep arms overhead, slight backbend, gaze up (Urdhva Hastasana)
EXHALE: Hinge at hips, fold forward, hands to floor or shins (Uttanasana)
INHALE: Lift chest halfway, flat back, fingertips on shins or floor (Ardha Uttanasana)
EXHALE: Step or jump back to Plank, lower through Chaturanga (elbows tight to ribs)
INHALE: Press through hands, lift chest into Upward Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
EXHALE: Lift hips, press back into Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana) - hold 5 breaths
Step or jump feet to hands, INHALE lift halfway, EXHALE fold
INHALE: Rise to standing, arms overhead, EXHALE: hands to heart center
Repeat sequence 5 times, finding a smooth rhythm
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Downward Dog to Pigeon Pose
exercises.notes: Square hips, fold forward, breathe into hip stretch
exercises.instruction:
From Downward Dog, lift right leg high
Bring right knee forward behind right wrist
Right shin can be parallel to front of mat (more advanced) or angled back toward left hip (modification)
Extend left leg straight back, top of foot on floor
Square hips toward front of mat—use a block under right hip if needed
Walk hands forward, fold chest toward floor
Hold for 2 minutes, breathing deeply into the hip
Press back to Downward Dog, shake out legs, repeat on left side
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Warrior I → Warrior II → Reverse Warrior
exercises.notes: Strong legs, open hips, flow with breath
exercises.instruction:
WARRIOR I: Step right foot forward into lunge, back foot angled 45°, hips squared forward, arms overhead, gaze up. Hold 30s.
WARRIOR II: Open hips and arms to side, back foot turns to 90°, front knee over ankle, arms parallel to floor, gaze over front fingers. Hold 30s.
REVERSE WARRIOR: Keep legs as is, flip front palm up, reach back and up, back hand slides down back leg, side body opens. Hold 30s.
Flow back through Warrior II to Warrior I
Step back to Mountain Pose, repeat entire sequence on left side
Maintain steady ujjayi breath throughout
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.notes: Initiate movement from pelvis, articulate through entire spine
exercises.instruction:
Start on hands and knees: wrists under shoulders, knees under hips
COW (Inhale): Tilt pelvis forward, drop belly, lift chest and gaze, shoulder blades draw together
CAT (Exhale): Tilt pelvis back, round spine toward ceiling, tuck chin, push floor away
Move slowly—feel each vertebra articulate
Let the breath initiate the movement, not the other way around
Continue for 10 full cycles
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.notes: Full surrender, deep belly breaths
exercises.instruction:
From hands and knees, sit hips back toward heels
Knees can be together (more back stretch) or wide apart (more hip stretch)
Walk arms forward, forehead rests on floor (or on stacked hands)
Let shoulders melt down away from ears
Breathe into your lower back and sides of ribcage
This is complete rest—let go of all tension
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.notes: Hinge from hips, not from lower back
exercises.instruction:
Sit with legs extended straight in front
Flex feet (toes point toward ceiling)
Inhale, lengthen spine, reach arms overhead
Exhale, hinge at hips (not waist), reach toward feet
Hold whatever you can reach: thighs, shins, ankles, or feet
Keep back as flat as possible—it's okay if knees bend slightly
Relax head and neck, breathe deeply
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Savasana (Corpse Pose)
exercises.notes: Complete stillness and surrender
exercises.instruction:
Lie flat on back, legs extended, feet fall open naturally
Arms at sides, palms facing up
Close eyes, release all muscular effort
Scan body for tension and consciously release it
Breathe naturally, observe without controlling
This is integration time—let the practice settle in
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Quad Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Start face down with roller under front of thighs, just above knees. Support upper body on forearms, engage core to protect lower back. Roll slowly from just above knee to hip crease. Rotate leg inward to target inner quad (vastus medialis), then rotate leg outward to target outer quad (vastus lateralis). When you find a tender spot, pause and breathe for 30s. Spend 1 minute on each leg.
exercises.notes: Roll slowly, rotate leg to hit all areas. Pause on tender spots for 30 seconds and breathe deeply.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for quadriceps muscles

exercises.name: IT Band Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Lie on your side with roller under outer thigh, just below hip. Bottom leg straight, top leg can stack on bottom (more pressure) or step in front (less pressure). Support yourself on bottom forearm. Roll from hip to just above knee (never roll over the knee joint). This area is often very tender—start with less pressure. Pause on tender spots, breathe and relax into the discomfort. Switch sides after 1 minute.
exercises.notes: Side-lying, control pressure with stacked legs. Start with less pressure as this area can be very tender.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for IT band

exercises.name: Glute Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on the roller, hands behind you for support. Cross right ankle over left knee (figure-4 position). Lean into right glute, finding tender spots. Make small movements or hold on tight spots. Target the piriformis by leaning deeper into the outer glute. Spend 30 seconds on each side.
exercises.notes: Cross ankle over knee for deeper release. Target the piriformis muscle.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for glutes and piriformis

exercises.name: Hamstring Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on roller positioned under back of thighs. Hands behind you for support, lift hips off ground. Roll from just below glutes to just above back of knee. Rotate leg inward to target inner hamstrings, then rotate leg outward to target outer hamstrings (biceps femoris). For more pressure, stack one leg on top of the other.
exercises.notes: Rotate leg to target different areas. 30 seconds on each leg.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for hamstring muscles

exercises.name: Lat Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Lie on your side with roller under armpit area. Extend bottom arm overhead, thumb pointing up. Roll from armpit down to mid-ribcage. Rotate slightly forward to target the lat more directly, or rotate slightly backward to target the teres major and rear delt. Keep core engaged, breathe through tender spots. Spend 1 minute on each side.
exercises.notes: Thumb up, arm extended overhead. Target lats and surrounding muscles.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for latissimus dorsi

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on floor, place roller behind you at mid-back level. Lie back with roller across upper-mid back. Interlace hands behind head to support neck. Lift hips slightly off ground. Roll from mid-back to upper back (not into neck). At tight spots, pause and extend back over the roller. Breathe deeply as you open the chest. Keep core engaged to protect lower back.
exercises.notes: Support head, extend over roller. Open the chest and improve thoracic spine mobility.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release and extension for thoracic spine

exercises.name: Sun Salutations
exercises.notes: Match breath to movement throughout
exercises.instruction:
Begin in Mountain Pose (Tadasana): Stand tall, feet together, arms at sides, weight evenly distributed
INHALE: Sweep arms overhead, slight backbend, gaze up (Urdhva Hastasana)
EXHALE: Hinge at hips, fold forward, hands to floor or shins (Uttanasana)
INHALE: Lift chest halfway, flat back, fingertips on shins or floor (Ardha Uttanasana)
EXHALE: Step or jump back to Plank, lower through Chaturanga (elbows tight to ribs)
INHALE: Press through hands, lift chest into Upward Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
EXHALE: Lift hips, press back into Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana) - hold 5 breaths
Step or jump feet to hands, INHALE lift halfway, EXHALE fold
INHALE: Rise to standing, arms overhead, EXHALE: hands to heart center
Repeat sequence 5 times, finding a smooth rhythm
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Downward Dog to Pigeon Pose
exercises.notes: Square hips, fold forward, breathe into hip stretch
exercises.instruction:
From Downward Dog, lift right leg high
Bring right knee forward behind right wrist
Right shin can be parallel to front of mat (more advanced) or angled back toward left hip (modification)
Extend left leg straight back, top of foot on floor
Square hips toward front of mat—use a block under right hip if needed
Walk hands forward, fold chest toward floor
Hold for 2 minutes, breathing deeply into the hip
Press back to Downward Dog, shake out legs, repeat on left side
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Warrior I → Warrior II → Reverse Warrior
exercises.notes: Strong legs, open hips, flow with breath
exercises.instruction:
WARRIOR I: Step right foot forward into lunge, back foot angled 45°, hips squared forward, arms overhead, gaze up. Hold 30s.
WARRIOR II: Open hips and arms to side, back foot turns to 90°, front knee over ankle, arms parallel to floor, gaze over front fingers. Hold 30s.
REVERSE WARRIOR: Keep legs as is, flip front palm up, reach back and up, back hand slides down back leg, side body opens. Hold 30s.
Flow back through Warrior II to Warrior I
Step back to Mountain Pose, repeat entire sequence on left side
Maintain steady ujjayi breath throughout
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.notes: Initiate movement from pelvis, articulate through entire spine
exercises.instruction:
Start on hands and knees: wrists under shoulders, knees under hips
COW (Inhale): Tilt pelvis forward, drop belly, lift chest and gaze, shoulder blades draw together
CAT (Exhale): Tilt pelvis back, round spine toward ceiling, tuck chin, push floor away
Move slowly—feel each vertebra articulate
Let the breath initiate the movement, not the other way around
Continue for 10 full cycles
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.notes: Full surrender, deep belly breaths
exercises.instruction:
From hands and knees, sit hips back toward heels
Knees can be together (more back stretch) or wide apart (more hip stretch)
Walk arms forward, forehead rests on floor (or on stacked hands)
Let shoulders melt down away from ears
Breathe into your lower back and sides of ribcage
This is complete rest—let go of all tension
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.notes: Hinge from hips, not from lower back
exercises.instruction:
Sit with legs extended straight in front
Flex feet (toes point toward ceiling)
Inhale, lengthen spine, reach arms overhead
Exhale, hinge at hips (not waist), reach toward feet
Hold whatever you can reach: thighs, shins, ankles, or feet
Keep back as flat as possible—it's okay if knees bend slightly
Relax head and neck, breathe deeply
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Savasana (Corpse Pose)
exercises.notes: Complete stillness and surrender
exercises.instruction:
Lie flat on back, legs extended, feet fall open naturally
Arms at sides, palms facing up
Close eyes, release all muscular effort
Scan body for tension and consciously release it
Breathe naturally, observe without controlling
This is integration time—let the practice settle in
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Quad Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Start face down with roller under front of thighs, just above knees. Support upper body on forearms, engage core to protect lower back. Roll slowly from just above knee to hip crease. Rotate leg inward to target inner quad (vastus medialis), then rotate leg outward to target outer quad (vastus lateralis). When you find a tender spot, pause and breathe for 30s. Spend 1 minute on each leg.
exercises.notes: Roll slowly, rotate leg to hit all areas. Pause on tender spots for 30 seconds and breathe deeply.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for quadriceps muscles

exercises.name: IT Band Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Lie on your side with roller under outer thigh, just below hip. Bottom leg straight, top leg can stack on bottom (more pressure) or step in front (less pressure). Support yourself on bottom forearm. Roll from hip to just above knee (never roll over the knee joint). This area is often very tender—start with less pressure. Pause on tender spots, breathe and relax into the discomfort. Switch sides after 1 minute.
exercises.notes: Side-lying, control pressure with stacked legs. Start with less pressure as this area can be very tender.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for IT band

exercises.name: Glute Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on the roller, hands behind you for support. Cross right ankle over left knee (figure-4 position). Lean into right glute, finding tender spots. Make small movements or hold on tight spots. Target the piriformis by leaning deeper into the outer glute. Spend 30 seconds on each side.
exercises.notes: Cross ankle over knee for deeper release. Target the piriformis muscle.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for glutes and piriformis

exercises.name: Hamstring Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on roller positioned under back of thighs. Hands behind you for support, lift hips off ground. Roll from just below glutes to just above back of knee. Rotate leg inward to target inner hamstrings, then rotate leg outward to target outer hamstrings (biceps femoris). For more pressure, stack one leg on top of the other.
exercises.notes: Rotate leg to target different areas. 30 seconds on each leg.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for hamstring muscles

exercises.name: Lat Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Lie on your side with roller under armpit area. Extend bottom arm overhead, thumb pointing up. Roll from armpit down to mid-ribcage. Rotate slightly forward to target the lat more directly, or rotate slightly backward to target the teres major and rear delt. Keep core engaged, breathe through tender spots. Spend 1 minute on each side.
exercises.notes: Thumb up, arm extended overhead. Target lats and surrounding muscles.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for latissimus dorsi

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Foam Roll
exercises.instruction: Sit on floor, place roller behind you at mid-back level. Lie back with roller across upper-mid back. Interlace hands behind head to support neck. Lift hips slightly off ground. Roll from mid-back to upper back (not into neck). At tight spots, pause and extend back over the roller. Breathe deeply as you open the chest. Keep core engaged to protect lower back.
exercises.notes: Support head, extend over roller. Open the chest and improve thoracic spine mobility.
exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release and extension for thoracic spine

exercises.name: Light Ladder Patterns
exercises.instruction:
Choose 1-2 patterns from the following options. Perform light, controlled movements focusing on rhythm and coordination:

1. SINGLE-IN RHYTHM RUN: Step one foot per square, alternating L-R-L-R. Feet land in center of each square. Keep steps short and quick, not bounding. Exit with smooth 5m acceleration. Cues: "Tap-tap-tap-tap", "Quiet feet, tall posture".

2. DOUBLE-IN QUICK STEPS: Step two feet in each square: L-R → L-R → L-R. Feet land under hips, not wide. Keep cadence fast but controlled. Avoid heel striking - stay on balls of feet. Cues: "Left-right, left-right", "Fast feet, slow body".

3. LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (WARM VERSION): Face sideways. Step in-in (lead foot first), then out-out. Example facing right: R-L in → R-L out. Feet stay parallel, hips square. Move down ladder without crossing legs. Cues: "Push the ground away", "Stay level - no bouncing".

4. ICKY SHUFFLE (LIGHT TEMPO): Step right foot in, left foot in, right foot out. Then left foot in, right foot in, left foot out. Pattern repeats diagonally through ladder. Keep steps small and rhythmic. Cues: "In-in-out, in-in-out", "Eyes up - see the field".

5. HOPSCOTCH (PREP VERSION): Two feet in → one foot out. Alternate landing foot each square. Example: both feet in → right foot out → both feet in → left foot out. Land softly on single leg. Cues: "Land under hips", "Don't let knee cave in".
exercises.definition: Prepares feet and nervous system for agility work. Focus on rhythm, coordination, and CNS wake-up. Intensity: smooth, not fast.
exercises.notes: Choose 1-2 patterns per session, rotating through all 5 over time. Keep it light and controlled. Focus on rhythm, not speed.

exercises.name: Cone Drills
exercises.notes: Zig-zag, 5-10-5 drills
exercises.instruction:
SETUP - Rotate through these patterns each set:

ZIG-ZAG PATTERN: Place 5-7 cones in a zig-zag pattern with 2-3 yards between each cone. Cones should be offset left-right-left-right to create sharp angles.

5-10-5 SHUTTLE: Place 3 cones in a straight line: start cone (0 yards), middle cone (5 yards from start), end cone (10 yards from middle = 15 yards total from start). Alternative: On a basketball court, use baseline as start (0 yards), free throw line extended (~5 yards), opposite free throw line extended (~10 yards), and opposite baseline (~15 yards).

EXECUTION:
- ZIG-ZAG: Sprint forward, cutting sharply around each cone. Lower hips and stay low through each cut. Push off the outside foot to accelerate out of each turn. Keep eyes up, see the next cone before you reach it.
- 5-10-5: Start at middle cone, sprint 5 yards to one side cone (touch ground), sprint 10 yards past middle to opposite cone (touch ground), sprint 5 yards back to middle. Focus on explosive direction changes, quick ground contacts, and staying low on turns.

Coaching cues: Lower hips on cuts, push off outside foot, stay low, quick direction changes, explosive acceleration out of each turn.
exercises.definition: Training movement: Cone Drills

exercises.name: 3 Min Continuous Ladder Flow
exercises.instruction:
Continuous agility flow - perform each segment for 30 seconds. Self-time each transition:

0:00-0:30 - FAST DOUBLE-IN: L-R in each square. Feet move like "machine gun taps". Stay tall, minimal vertical bounce. Exit with 3m burst. Rugby transfer: acceleration after footwork.

0:30-1:00 - LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (DEFENSIVE DRIFT): Face sideways. Lead foot steps in first: R-L in → R-L out. Keep shoulders square. Add 2m "tackle finish" at end. Rugby transfer: drift defense, tracking attackers.

1:00-1:30 - ICKY SHUFFLE + SIDESTEP EXIT: In-in-out pattern through ladder. At end, plant outside foot (right or left). Explode into sidestep opposite direction. Rugby transfer: evasive footwork, fend setup.

1:30-2:00 - REACTIVE CALL PATTERN: Self-call pattern - call out to yourself: "IN" → single-in (L-R-L-R), "OUT" → double-out (feet outside ladder each square), "LEFT" or "RIGHT" → lateral shuffle (no crossing feet). Rugby transfer: decision-making under movement.

2:00-2:30 - CROSSOVER STEP (CUTTING PREP): Step across body into each square. Example: right foot crosses over left into square. Keep hips facing forward. Add 3m acceleration at exit. Rugby transfer: sharp angle changes, line breaks.
exercises.definition: Foot-speed, reactive agility, rugby transfer. Intensity: 70-90%
exercises.notes: Self-time each 30-second segment. Focus on foot-speed and rugby-specific movement patterns. Smooth transitions between patterns.

Flow back through Warrior II to Warrior I
Step back to Mountain Pose, repeat entire sequence on left side
Maintain steady ujjayi breath throughout

Pause on tender spots, breathe and relax into the discomfort. Switch sides after 1 minute.

exercises.name: Light Ladder Patterns
exercises.instruction:
Choose 1-2 patterns from the following options. Perform light, controlled movements focusing on rhythm and coordination:

1. SINGLE-IN RHYTHM RUN: Step one foot per square, alternating L-R-L-R. Feet land in center of each square. Keep steps short and quick, not bounding. Exit with smooth 5m acceleration. Cues: "Tap-tap-tap-tap", "Quiet feet, tall posture".

2. DOUBLE-IN QUICK STEPS: Step two feet in each square: L-R → L-R → L-R. Feet land under hips, not wide. Keep cadence fast but controlled. Avoid heel striking - stay on balls of feet. Cues: "Left-right, left-right", "Fast feet, slow body".

3. LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (WARM VERSION): Face sideways. Step in-in (lead foot first), then out-out. Example facing right: R-L in → R-L out. Feet stay parallel, hips square. Move down ladder without crossing legs. Cues: "Push the ground away", "Stay level - no bouncing".

4. ICKY SHUFFLE (LIGHT TEMPO): Step right foot in, left foot in, right foot out. Then left foot in, right foot in, left foot out. Pattern repeats diagonally through ladder. Keep steps small and rhythmic. Cues: "In-in-out, in-in-out", "Eyes up - see the field".

5. HOPSCOTCH (PREP VERSION): Two feet in → one foot out. Alternate landing foot each square. Example: both feet in → right foot out → both feet in → left foot out. Land softly on single leg. Cues: "Land under hips", "Don't let knee cave in".
exercises.definition: Prepares feet and nervous system for agility work. Focus on rhythm, coordination, and CNS wake-up. Intensity: smooth, not fast.
exercises.notes: Choose 1-2 patterns per session, rotating through all 5 over time. Keep it light and controlled. Focus on rhythm, not speed.

exercises.name: 3-Min Continuous Rugby Agility Flow
exercises.instruction:
Continuous agility flow - perform each segment for 30 seconds. Self-time each transition:

0:00-0:30 - FAST DOUBLE-IN: L-R in each square. Feet move like "machine gun taps". Stay tall, minimal vertical bounce. Exit with 3m burst. Rugby transfer: acceleration after footwork.

0:30-1:00 - LATERAL 2-IN 2-OUT (DEFENSIVE DRIFT): Face sideways. Lead foot steps in first: R-L in → R-L out. Keep shoulders square. Add 2m "tackle finish" at end. Rugby transfer: drift defense, tracking attackers.

1:00-1:30 - ICKY SHUFFLE + SIDESTEP EXIT: In-in-out pattern through ladder. At end, plant outside foot (right or left). Explode into sidestep opposite direction. Rugby transfer: evasive footwork, fend setup.

1:30-2:00 - REACTIVE CALL PATTERN: Self-call pattern - call out to yourself: "IN" → single-in (L-R-L-R), "OUT" → double-out (feet outside ladder each square), "LEFT" or "RIGHT" → lateral shuffle (no crossing feet). Rugby transfer: decision-making under movement.

2:00-2:30 - CROSSOVER STEP (CUTTING PREP): Step across body into each square. Example: right foot crosses over left into square. Keep hips facing forward. Add 3m acceleration at exit. Rugby transfer: sharp angle changes, line breaks.
exercises.definition: Foot-speed, reactive agility, rugby transfer. Intensity: 70-90%
exercises.notes: Self-time each 30-second segment. Focus on foot-speed and rugby-specific movement patterns. Smooth transitions between patterns.

EXHALE: Hinge at hips, fold forward, hands to floor or shins (Uttanasana)
INHALE: Lift chest halfway, flat back, fingertips on shins or floor (Ardha Uttanasana)
EXHALE: Step or jump back to Plank, lower through Chaturanga (elbows tight to ribs)
INHALE: Press through hands, lift chest into Upward Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
EXHALE: Lift hips, press back into Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana) - hold 5 breaths
Step or jump feet to hands, INHALE lift halfway, EXHALE fold
INHALE: Rise to standing, arms overhead, EXHALE: hands to heart center

Extend left leg straight back, top of foot on floor

Hold for 2 minutes, breathing deeply into the hip
Press back to Downward Dog, shake out legs, repeat on left side

exercises.name: Warrior I → Warrior II → Reverse Warrior
exercises.notes: Strong legs, open hips, flow with breath

WARRIOR I: Step right foot forward into lunge, back foot angled 45°, hips squared forward, arms overhead, gaze up. Hold 30s.
WARRIOR II: Open hips and arms to side, back foot turns to 90°, front knee over ankle, arms parallel to floor, gaze over front fingers. Hold 30s.
REVERSE WARRIOR: Keep legs as is, flip front palm up, reach back and up, back hand slides down back leg, side body opens. Hold 30s.
Flow back through Warrior II to Warrior I
Step back to Mountain Pose, repeat entire sequence on left side
Maintain steady ujjayi breath throughout
exercises.definition: Dynamic stretching sequence that improves flexibility, balance, and body awareness.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.notes: Initiate movement from pelvis, articulate through entire spine

CAT (Exhale): Tilt pelvis back, round spine toward ceiling, tuck chin, push floor away
Move slowly—feel each vertebra articulate
Let the breath initiate the movement, not the other way around
Continue for 10 full cycles

exercises.instruction:

Scan body for tension and consciously release it

exercises.instruction: Start face down with roller under front of thighs, just above knees. Support upper body on forearms, engage core to protect lower back. Roll slowly from just above knee to hip crease. Rotate leg inward to target inner quad (vastus medialis), then rotate leg outward to target outer quad (vastus lateralis). When you find a tender spot, pause and breathe for 30s. Spend 1 minute on each leg.

exercises.definition: Self-myofascial release for IT band

exercises.name: Hamstring Foam Roll

exercises.name: Contact Drills
exercises.notes: Develop contact strength, collision preparation, and tackle/ruck/maul movement patterns. Choose field or gym option based on available equipment.
exercises.instruction:
SETUP:

FIELD OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Tackle Bag Available): Place tackle bag on ground. Drive bag forward 10-15m, simulate clearing ruck position (low, driving with shoulders), walk back dragging bag. Repeat for 90s.
- OPTION 2 (No Tackle Bag): Set up 3-4 cones in a line, 5m apart. Sprint to first cone → drop into low tackle position (one knee to ground, body low) → get up explosively → sprint to next cone → repeat. At last cone, add 5 burpees then return to start.
- OPTION 3 (Ruck Simulation Circuit): Place 2-3 cones in staggered pattern. Sprint to cone → drop into low body position (simulate ruck entry - hips low, shoulders forward) → drive forward 3 steps pushing through → sprint to next cone → repeat for 90s.

GYM OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Sled Available): Load sled with 50-70% bodyweight. Drive sled forward 20m with low body position (hips below shoulders, forward lean). Walk back. Repeat for 90s. Focus on powerful leg drive and maintaining contact position.
- OPTION 2 (Sandbag/Heavy Bag): Hold heavy sandbag or heavy bag in bear hug position (arms wrapped around). Walk forward 10-15m, maintain tight grip. Drop bag, sprint back 10m, return to bag. Repeat for 90s. Simulates carrying opponent in contact.
- OPTION 3 (Battle Ropes + Burpees): 30s battle ropes (waves, alternating waves) → 3 explosive burpees (simulates getting up from ground after contact) → 30s battle ropes → 3 burpees. Repeat for full 90s. Rest is built into transitions.
- OPTION 4 (Sledgehammer + Tire): Strike tire with sledgehammer from various angles: 10 overhead strikes, 10 side strikes (left), 10 side strikes (right), 10 low strikes (simulating ruck clearing). Repeat sequence for 90s. Focus on explosive, controlled strikes.

EXECUTION:
- Maintain low body position throughout (hips below shoulders)
- Drive through legs, not just upper body
- Keep core braced for contact simulation
- Focus on explosive power through contact
- For field options: Make movements realistic to rugby contact situations
- For gym options: Use heavy enough load to challenge, but maintain proper form

exercises.name: Scrummaging
exercises.notes: Develop scrum-specific strength: neck stability, core stability, lower body drive, isometric holds, and posterior chain power. Choose option based on available equipment.
exercises.instruction:
SETUP:

FIELD OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Scrum Machine Available): Set up in scrum position against machine. On "engage", push hard against machine for 30s. Maintain proper scrum position: back flat, head up, core braced, legs driving. Rest 120s between sets.
- OPTION 2 (Partner Available): Partner stands behind you. You're in scrum position (low stance, back flat, arms extended). Partner pushes against your shoulders with moderate resistance. Hold position and resist for 30s. Focus on leg drive and core stability.
- OPTION 3 (Wall Scrum Hold): Face wall, get into scrum position (bent knees, back flat, arms extended to wall). Push against wall with shoulders and arms for 30s isometric hold. Keep legs driving, core braced.

GYM OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Trap Bar Deadlift Hold): Load trap bar with 70-85% 1RM. Lift bar to standing position. Hold in "up" position (knees slightly bent, hips extended, core braced, shoulders back) for 30s. This develops scrum lockout strength and posterior chain stability. Lower with control, rest 120s.
- OPTION 2 (Farmers Walk + Overhead Hold): Pick up heavy dumbbells/kettlebells (50-70% bodyweight total). Walk forward 15m with farmers walk. At end, press weights overhead and hold for 15s (or remaining time). Walk back. This develops grip, core stability, and shoulder/neck stability (key for scrum). Rest 120s.
- OPTION 3 (Landmine Row + Hold): Set up landmine with heavy load (handle at low position). Row from low position (simulating scrum pull) to chest. Hold at top position for 15s. Lower slowly. Repeat for 30s total. This simulates the pulling and holding component of scrummaging.
- OPTION 4 (Wall Sit + Resistance Band): Place resistance band around knees. Get into wall sit position (back against wall, knees at 90°, hips level with knees). Push knees out against band continuously while holding wall sit for 30s. This develops leg drive and hip stability crucial for scrum engagement.
- OPTION 5 (Barbell Hip Thrust + Hold): Load barbell with 70-85% 1RM. Perform hip thrust. At top position (hips fully extended), hold for 5 seconds. Lower slowly. Repeat for 30s total (approximately 4-6 reps with holds). This develops posterior chain drive essential for scrum power.

EXECUTION:
- Maintain proper scrum position: back flat, core braced, head in neutral position
- Drive through legs, not just upper body
- Keep shoulders back and down (retracted)
- Focus on isometric strength and stability
- For holds: Breathe normally but maintain tension
- For walking exercises: Maintain tall posture and engaged core
exercises.definition: Develops scrum-specific strength including neck stability, core stability, lower body drive, isometric holds, and posterior chain power. Essential for rugby forwards' scrum performance and collision preparation.

exercises.name: Situational Conditioning Blocks
exercises.notes: Simulate game-like metabolic demands with multi-directional movements, repeated high-intensity efforts, and varied recovery periods. Mimics rugby match conditions: bursts of high intensity followed by active recovery.
exercises.intensity: Variable (70-95% effort with active recovery periods)
exercises.instruction:
SETUP:

FIELD OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Multi-Directional Shuttle Circuit): Set up 4 cones in a rectangle: Start cone, forward cone (10m), side cone (10m left), return cone. Pattern: Sprint forward 10m → backpedal 5m → lateral shuffle left 10m → lateral shuffle right 10m → sprint forward to start. Repeat for 5 min with varied intensities (hard sprint, moderate shuffle, active recovery walk).
- OPTION 2 (Field Movement Patterns): Set up cones in pattern simulating game scenarios. Pattern: Sprint 20m → jog 10m → sprint 10m → walk 5m → repeat. Vary the pattern each set (add cuts, lateral movements, changes of direction). Use field markers (22m, 10m lines) if on rugby field. Total 5 min per set.
- OPTION 3 (Ladder + Cone Combination): Place agility ladder at one end, 3-4 cones in pattern 10m away. Ladder footwork (30s - fast double-in, icky shuffle, lateral patterns) → sprint to first cone → cut left → sprint to second cone → cut right → sprint to third cone → jog back to ladder. Repeat for 5 min. Vary ladder patterns each round.

GYM OPTIONS:
- OPTION 1 (Assault Bike + KB Swings Circuit): 30s assault bike max effort (90-95% effort) → 30s KB swings (moderate, 20-24kg) → 30s active recovery (easy bike or walk) → repeat. Continue this 90-second cycle for 5 min total (approximately 3-4 cycles). Focus on maintaining intensity during work periods.
- OPTION 2 (Rower + Battle Ropes Circuit): 1 min rower at hard pace (80-85% effort, focus on power per stroke) → 30s battle ropes (varied patterns: waves, alternating, slams) → 30s rest (stand, breathe, prepare) → repeat. Continue for 5 min total (approximately 3 cycles). Mimics game work:rest ratios.
- OPTION 3 (Heavy Circuit): Heavy sled push (15m with 60-70% bodyweight) → heavy farmers walk (15m, 50-60% bodyweight each hand) → 10 burpees → 30s rest (walk, breathe) → repeat. Continue for 5 min total. Focus on maintaining form under fatigue.
- OPTION 4 (Treadmill/Spin Interval Block): Set treadmill or bike. Pattern: 2 min @ 70% (moderate pace, "defensive line pace") → 30s sprint @ 90-95% (all-out effort, "breakaway sprint") → 30s walk/easy spin (active recovery) → repeat. Continue for 5 min total. This mimics game pacing with bursts of high intensity.
- OPTION 5 (Mixed Equipment Circuit): If multiple pieces available, rotate: 45s rower → 45s assault bike → 45s battle ropes → 45s burpees → 30s rest. Repeat for 5 min. Variety helps maintain engagement and simulates game unpredictability.

EXECUTION:
- Work periods should feel challenging (hard to very hard)
- Active recovery periods should be truly easy (walk, easy bike, standing rest)
- Vary movement patterns and intensities throughout the 5 min block
- Focus on maintaining technique under fatigue (simulates game conditions)
- Use timer or clock to track 5 min blocks accurately
- Each set should challenge you, but be repeatable for 3 total sets

INTENSITY GUIDELINES:
- High intensity periods: 85-95% effort (should feel like game-breaking sprint, tackle, or collision)
- Moderate periods: 70-80% effort (sustained defensive work, support running)
- Active recovery: 40-50% effort (easy jog, walk, or complete rest)
- Heart rate zones: Should fluctuate between Zone 4-5 (high intensity) and Zone 2 (recovery)

exercises.name: Slow Nasal Breathing
exercises.instruction: Stand or sit comfortably. Breathe slowly and deeply through nose
exercises.definition: Promotes parasympathetic activation and recovery
exercises.notes: Slow, controlled breathing through nose. Focus on relaxation.

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Strap Stretch
exercises.instruction: Lie on back. Loop band or strap around one foot. Keep leg straight, pull leg toward you until you feel stretch
exercises.definition: Stretches hamstring muscles
exercises.notes: Keep leg straight. Pull gently until you feel stretch. Don't force it.
formCues: Feel stretch in back of thigh

exercises.name: Chest Opener Stretch (Hands Behind Back)
exercises.instruction: Stand tall. Interlace fingers behind back, straighten arms, lift chest. Feel stretch in front of shoulders and chest
exercises.definition: Stretches pectoral muscles and improves shoulder mobility
exercises.notes: Keep shoulders down. Don't force the stretch.
formCues: Feel stretch in front of shoulders

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip External Rotation Stretch
exercises.instruction: Sit on floor. Front leg bent at 90° with shin parallel to body. Back leg bent at 90° with shin perpendicular. Lean forward over front leg
exercises.definition: Stretches external hip rotators and improves hip mobility
exercises.notes: Keep both legs at 90°. Lean forward to increase stretch. This is a deep stretch.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.instruction: Start on hands and knees. Arch back, lift head (cow), then round spine, tuck chin (cat). Flow between positions
exercises.definition: Mobilizes entire spine and improves flexibility
exercises.notes: Move slowly and smoothly. Feel each vertebra articulate.
formCues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips
COW: Arch back, lift head and tail
CAT: Round spine, tuck chin and tail

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.instruction: From hands and knees, sit hips back toward heels. Walk arms forward, rest forehead on floor
exercises.definition: Stretches lower back and promotes relaxation
exercises.notes: Knees can be together or wide apart. Focus on deep breathing and relaxation.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
exercises.instruction: Stand tall, hinge at hips, fold forward. Let head hang, reach toward floor or shins
exercises.definition: Stretches hamstrings and decompresses spine
exercises.notes: Hinge from hips, not waist. Keep knees slightly bent if needed.

exercises.name: Chest Opener Stretch
exercises.instruction: Stand or sit. Interlace fingers behind back, straighten arms, lift chest. Feel stretch in front of shoulders and chest
exercises.definition: Stretches pectoral muscles and improves shoulder mobility
exercises.notes: Keep shoulders down. Don't force the stretch.
formCues: Feel stretch in front of shoulders

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.instruction: Kneel on one knee, other foot forward. Tuck pelvis, squeeze glute of back leg. Lean forward slightly
exercises.definition: Stretches hip flexors and improves hip mobility
exercises.notes: Tuck pelvis first, then lean. This is key for proper hip flexor stretch.
formCues: Feel stretch in front of hip
